   MINUTES OF THE REGULAR MEETING
  CITY OF NORWALK PARKS AND RECREATION COMMISSION
  December 11, 2025

Chairperson Victor H. Juan called the meeting to order at 6:08 p.m.

Commission members present were Anthony Armendarez, Maria Carbajal, Alejandra
Hernandez, David King, and Briana Martinez. Commissioners Monique Yanez,
Francisco Berberabe, Antoinette Moreno, and Don Valenzuela were absent.
Staff present included Director of Recreation and Park Services Allan Perdomo,
Superintendent Sonia Batres, Recreation Supervisor Rosie Lozoya, and Office
Assistant III Lorraine Mendoza.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES

Commissioner Martinez motioned to accept the November 13, 2025, meeting minutes.
Commissioner Armendarez seconded the motion. All in favor.
REPORTS

Las Posadas 2026 Food Discussion Results

Recreation Supervisor Lozoya presented the results of the Las Posadas food
discussion, highlighting the top selections for tamales, sweet bread, and buñuelos. The
winners were Ms. Preciado for Best Tamales, La Corona Bakery for Best Pan Dulce,
and Isme Martinez for Best Buñuelos. Based on these results, staff will purchase 3,000
tamales, 500 sweet breads, and 500 buñuelos for the 2026 Las Posadas event. The
festive evening will also include live music, food trucks, and refreshments for the
community to enjoy.

Summer 2026 Concert Performances – Genre Schedule

Recreation Supervisor Lozoya reviewed the proposed genre schedule for the 2026
Summer Concerts, Front Street Fridays, and the Independence Day Festival,
incorporating recommendations from the Parks and Recreation Commissioners. The
genres presented included rock, mariachi, rhythm and blues, tribute bands, freestyle,
reggae, dance music, banda, 80’s, 90’s, and classical. Based on Commissioner and
staff input, the 2026 concert schedule will feature a rock band on July 3 for the
Independence Day Festival. The Summer Concert Series will include a tribute band on
July 8, freestyle music on July 22, and mariachi on August 5. Front Street Friday events
will feature Top 40 music on July 17, dance music on July 31, and 80’s music on
National Night Out, August 14. Recreation Supervisor Lozoya advised that all bands are
subject to change based on availability and cost. Chairperson Juan motioned to accept
the recommended genre schedule. Commissioner King seconded the motion. All in
favor.
 Minutes of the Regular Meeting
Parks and Recreation Commission Meeting
December 11, 2025

Norwalk Park Master Plan Summary Report

Director Perdomo provided a brief update on the Norwalk Park Master Plan. He
reported that Community Outreach Meetings were held on June 25, June 28, July 17,
and July 30 to share information and gather input on the project plan. The final master
plan has since been approved and was submitted in August 2025 for $6 million in grant
funding through the Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF). A site visit with a
California State Parks representative took place on November 4, 2025, and the City of
Norwalk is currently a finalist for the grant. A tentative award announcement is
anticipated in January or February 2026. Director Perdomo also shared plans to apply
for additional funding through the Proposition 4 Grant Program in 2026 and noted a
pending funding request with the River Mountain Conservancy Grant. Commissioner
Hernandez asked several questions, which were addressed by Director Perdomo.

Park Projects Monthly Update

Director Perdomo provided an update on recently completed and ongoing park projects
throughout the City. Complimentary Wi-Fi and surveillance camera installations have
been completed citywide in all parks. At Robert White Park, a modular restroom, a new
playground, and the City’s first Dog Park have been installed. Gerdes Park received
new flooring, fresh paint, and sound panels to support the Adaptive Recreation
Program. In addition to Robert White Park, new playgrounds have been installed at
Vista Verde Park, New River Park, and Holifield Park. Pour-in-place playground
surfacing has been completed at Gerdes Park, Glazier Park, Lakeside Park, and
Ramona Park. Snack bar renovations were completed at Gerdes Park, Lakeside Park,
and Zimmerman Park, and new park pergolas were constructed at Gerdes Park, New
River Park, and Vista Verde Park. Welded park signage has also been installed
citywide.

Director Perdomo also highlighted projects currently in progress, including ball field
lighting improvements at Holifield Park, Zimmerman Park, Gerdes Park, Ramona Park,
and Lakeside Park. Solar array installations are underway at the Norwalk Arts and
Sports Complex, the Aquatics Pavilion, and Well 10.

Community engagement meetings are planned for January and February 2026 to
discuss the Holifield Park and Robert White Park Master Plans. Holifield Park
improvements are being funded through Measure A T.A.P. funds, with additional grant
funding to be pursued. Planned renovations at Robert White Park include irrigation,
electrical upgrades, parking lot improvements, and construction of a block wall.

Lastly, Director Perdomo provided a brief history and overview of the Hermosillo Park
Rehabilitation, Stormwater Capture, and Infiltration Project, including projected costs

and a final plan anticipated in 2028 that will include full basketball and handball courts.
Community Open Houses for Hermosillo Park will be held at Sanchez Elementary
School on the third Wednesday of every other month, beginning November 19 at 6:30
p.m. Commissioners had some questions that were addressed by Director Perdomo.

STAFF COMMENTS

Director Perdomo wished the Parks and Recreation Commissioners a Happy Holiday
and expressed his appreciation for the opportunity to work with them. He also
announced the upcoming Las Posadas event, scheduled for January 3, 2026, at the
Norwalk Arts and Sports Complex. Director Perdomo shared his confidence in the
progress of the Hermosillo Park Project and reassured the Commissioners that parking
concerns at Robert White Park remain on his radar. He added that signups for this
year’s 5K Run are already underway.

COMMISISONER’S COMMENTS

Commissioner Armendarez – Shared he is happy with the new Hermosillo Park
Project Plan. Growing up in the area, he knows firsthand it was not always a safe place,
happy that law enforcement and city staff will be on site. Would like to be included in
meeting notices and updates and plans to attend future meetings. Thanked Director
Perdomo for hosting the Hermosillo Park meeting and for speaking to the crowd at the
groundbreaking. Also looking forward to the Las Posadas and thanked staff for a
wonderful Holiday Festival and Tree Lighting Ceremony. The Mayor Re-Organization
Event was fun and cannot wait for next year.

Commissioner Martinez – She stated that it has been a great year and thanked
Director Perdomo for his efforts in securing grants that made the park projects possible.
She expressed surprise at the community complaints regarding the Hermosillo Park
Project and commended Director Perdomo for doing an excellent job addressing the
crowd at the groundbreaking. She also praised the Holiday Festival and Tree Lighting
Ceremony, noting she was impressed with the planning and layout, and thanked staff
for their outstanding work.

Commissioner Carbajal – Gave her insight on the Hermosillo Park Project, hopes it
will be accessible to the surrounding community. She hopes the City of Norwalk
continues to keep up the good work and thanked staff for all they do. Mentioned she
attended the nice holiday event at the Norwalk Square. She will be out of town during
the Las Posadas Event.

Commissioner King – Feels 2025 has been a successful year and loved the 5K Event
and cannot wait for the next 5K. Appreciates all the new lighting at the parks. Thought

that the Don Knabe Golf Event was fun as well as the Holiday Festival and Tree
Lighting Ceremony. Made some suggestions for next year’s event.

Commissioner Hernandez – Stated it has been an eventful year and complimented
the City on handling all this year’s trials and tribulations with grace. Made comments on
the Hermosillo Park Project and hopes the soccer fields are an asset to the surrounding
community. Advised she is willing to help in any way and thanked the staff for all their
hard work and dedication.

Chairperson Juan – He stated that the City’s social media presence has improved and
that presentations continue to get better. He expressed appreciation for the increased
involvement of the Commissioners and shared his hope that, despite staff transitions,
projects will not be left unfinished. He suggested hosting a Hawaiian Festival and
concluded by wishing everyone happy holidays and thanking all for their hard work and
dedication.

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
NEXT MEETING
January 8, 2026

There being no further business to discuss, Chairperson Juan motioned to adjourn the
meeting. Seconded by Commissioner King. All in favor. The meeting was adjourned at
7:26 p.m.

Respectfully submitted,
